anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after session-stage routing, gates, browser signal preparation, asynchronous hand-off and event bridging, whose own body constructs the target observable browser_fp fingerprint hash value rather than merely collecting signals, dispatching control, packaging the result, formatting a sink payload, or emitting it to the console.

primary_anchor.source_export: private helper reached through exported u(config)
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the target browser_fp by composing prepared browser signal text, materializing signal bytes and encoding the observable fp_ hash string.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle. Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function, not source_function.
A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label and is not a default answer-space key.
Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from signal collection, phase gates, asynchronous transport, event bridging, fold-only helpers, wrappers, sink formatting and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

role_oracle.why: Constructs the target browser_fp by composing signal text, materializing bytes and returning the encoded fp_ hash.
Materializes the Uint8Array that carries transformed browser signal lanes into the fingerprint hash encoder.
Folds the target byte array into the observed fp_ base36 browser fingerprint string.
Generic lane mixing utility directly used while materializing bytes for the target fingerprint.
Orders and joins prepared browser signal fields before byte materialization.
Factory that returns a closure calling the private fingerprint anchor with a selected slot config.
Carries the prepared packet through microtask, timer, mutation and animation-frame boundaries before fingerprinting.
Transfers the packet through the local CustomEvent bridge on the target path.
Emits an already constructed browser_fp value to console.log under the target action.
Formats an already constructed browser_fp value into the target console payload.
Boot-time vendor-like FNV digest decoy; it runs during mount but does not feed the target browser_fp field.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_default_agent_corpus; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The final console sink and payload wrapper emit an already constructed browser_fp value.
The exported factory only binds slot config and returns a closure; it should not outrank the private anchor function.
Session gates, state-machine routing, async hand-off and event bridging are path-critical preparation, not the target value constructor.
Boot-time vendor digests and fingerprint.shadow.action debug objects are decoys and do not feed the target browser_fp field.
debug_hints_private: The primary source-side anchor is deriveBrowserFingerprint in src/z0/k7/q3/t9.js.
The target field name and action are assembled at the sink from character-code arrays.
Source paths are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default answer space.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span; answer_function matches the function declaration in that captured bundle slice.
Returned span maps to a target-specific helper such as materializeSignalBytes or encodeFingerprintHash.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the browser fingerprint value construction path.
Returned span maps to a path-critical routing, async, bridge, wrapper or final payload function.
Returned span maps to an off-chain decoy or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
